key_insight: Ring-shaped sidewall barriers can suppress wall modes in confined rotating turbulent convection, reducing sidewall-driven flow structures and bringing the system closer to bulk-like behavior.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical way to improve experimental access to extreme rotating-convection regimes by limiting sidewall bias in heat transport and flow organization.
method: Combined laboratory experiments with direct numerical simulations in cylindrical rotating-convection cells.
Tested one or two ring-shaped sidewall barriers with varying barrier width, conductivity, and geometry.
Compared wall-mode strength, heat transport, radial jets, and mean azimuthal flow with and without barriers.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that barriers suppress near-wall vertical-velocity maxima, weaken wall-mode heat-transport enhancement, and reduce radial jets and boundary zonal flow, especially when the barrier width matches the wall-mode scale or a second barrier is added.
watch_item: Barrier effects are local: they can create baroclinic flow near the barrier faces and measurements must avoid the immediate barrier vicinity to assess true suppression.
paper_title: Suppressing wall modes in confined rotating turbulent convection
